correctness.rationale: For the exact Eq. (4) projection, M-matrix inversion and a column-sum computation give an iff criterion for mean preservation of every innate profile. Each role deviation balances its hyperedge automatically, giving the signed incidence nullspace. Spanning-forest rank proves the cycle-space dimension, and strict positivity of roles gives the exact feasible amplitude on a single cycle. Doubly stochastic Jensen contraction and the full symbolic four-node inverse prove the polarization claims. The packaged checker passes exact symbolic identities and 175 rational-hypergraph tests; such tests corroborate but do not establish universal quantification.

value.rationale: The primary mathematical question is structural: which asymmetric higher-order influence assignments conserve aggregate opinion in this model? An exact iff in incidence-cycle topology resolves it for arbitrary hypergraphs, with forest rigidity and a sharp role-feasibility boundary. The smallest overlapping three-person groups show neutral directed influence can either increase or decrease polarization compared with the uniform-role baseline. This corrects a tempting overgeneralization of the empirical directed-versus-symmetric comparison and is of natural future use in constrained network design; no claim is made to empirical or nonlinear generalization.
